@kpd_wrangler, I did read the changelog. I’ve now found the cause in PR #812: `LineList.__init__` changed its default `wave_frame` from `'air'` in 2.4.3 to `'vacuum'` in 2.5.0. My spectra are calibrated in air, so the default rest wavelengths no longer match the wavelength frame of the data.

At H-alpha, the vacuum-to-air wavelength ratio is about 1.00028, consistent with the redshift offset I reported (roughly 83 km/s). The workaround for my air-calibrated spectra is to set the frame explicitly:

`LineList(..., wave_frame='air')`

I’m frustrated that the thread was marked solved and the problem attributed to my calibration without testing the change. I spent two days thinking my wavelength calibration was broken and re-reduced arc lamps for 40 spectra unnecessarily. The 2.5.0 changelog describes #812 as a “refactor”; it doesn’t say the default changed, and there was no deprecation warning. I don’t think someone reading that entry could reasonably infer this behavior.

“Works for me” isn’t a test of this case. For example, data already in vacuum wavelengths or radio data may not show the same difference as my air-calibrated optical spectra. Also, m_okonkwo reported a similar offset in this thread, so I’m not the only person seeing one, though we haven’t established whether theirs has the same cause.

Could a maintainer please reopen this thread? It would also help to add an explicit line to CHANGES.md about the default changing from air to vacuum, or issue a warning when `wave_frame` isn’t set. That would make the behavior much easier to catch for anyone upgrading with an existing configuration.
